source_name: ЕСЈН — Електронски систем за јавни набавки (e-nabavki.gov.mk, public access)
why_relevant: Central, legally mandated national e-procurement system of North Macedonia. All contracting authorities (ministries, NBRSM, municipalities, public enterprises) must publish procurement plans, contract notices, tender documentation, award decisions and concluded contracts here. For A6 this is the densest single source of vendor/competitor names, contract subjects (core banking, card systems, POS/ATM, payment infrastructure) and contract values.

source_name: ЕСЈН — Реализирани договори / преглед по институција (InstitutionGridData)
why_relevant: Institution-scoped grid of realised/executed contracts. Lets you pivot from a contracting authority (e.g. НБРСМ, Царинска управа, Министерство за финансии) to the full list of its executed contracts and suppliers — ideal for building a vendor-share picture per authority rather than per tender.

source_name: ЕСЈН — Досие на постапка (dosieNotificationForACPP.aspx)
why_relevant: Per-procedure dossier page carrying the notice, tender documentation, the одлука за избор (award decision) and the concluded contract. This is the page that actually names the winning economic operator and value — the atomic evidence unit for A6 vendor/competitor mapping.

source_name: ЕСЈН internal web services (/services/*.asmx)
why_relevant: The portal's SPA is backed by ASMX web services; these are the machine-friendly entry points behind the grids. Discovering the notice/contract-list service would remove the need for brittle DOM scraping and give structured JSON for the whole A6 pipeline.

source_name: ЕСЈН тест/обука околина (tea.e-nabavki.gov.mk)
why_relevant: Training/test instance of the same platform. Useful for safely mapping the URL scheme, form parameters and service calls of the production portal without hammering production, and for detecting platform version changes.

source_name: Биро за јавни набавки (БЈН) — официјален сајт
source_subtype: regulator website / methodology and annual reports
why_relevant: The regulator/operator of the ESJN. Publishes the legal framework, manuals, annual reports on public procurement in RSM and statistics — the map of who must publish what, which underpins any completeness claim about A6 evidence.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Биро за јавни набавки / Е-јавни набавки
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance page describing the BJN's status and the ESJN's modules (planned procurements, notices, awarded contracts, realised contracts). Authoritative description of what each module contains — needed to target the right module for award evidence.

source_name: Државна комисија за жалби по јавни набавки (ДКЖЈН) — жалби и одлуки
why_relevant: Appeals body publishing filed complaints and its decisions. Complaints in IT/payments tenders reveal the losing bidders (i.e. the competitor set that does not appear in an award notice), disputed technical specifications, and sometimes annulled awards that would otherwise be miscounted as wins.

source_name: Државен завод за ревизија (ДЗР) — ревизорски извештаи по институција
why_relevant: State Audit Office reports on individual institutions (the term/412 page is the NBRSM taxonomy page). Audit reports frequently narrate IT and payment-system procurements in detail — vendor names, contract values, multi-year maintenance arrangements — including procedures poorly documented on the ESJN.

source_name: Народна банка на РСМ — Јавни набавки
why_relevant: The central bank's own procurement page. NBRSM procures the national payment infrastructure (RTGS/МИПС, instant payments, registers), so its notices and contracts are the highest-value single stream in this cell for payments-infrastructure vendors.

source_name: Портал за отворени податоци — data.gov.mk (склучени договори од ЕСЈН)
why_relevant: National open-data portal; the ESJN 'concluded contracts' module is published here in machine-readable form (the portal redirects to the download location). If the bulk file exists and is current, it is by far the cheapest structured route to the full award/vendor dataset instead of scraping.

source_name: Министерство за дигитална трансформација — Отворени податоци / Јавни набавки
why_relevant: The ministry that owns the open-data policy and is itself a contracting authority for state digitalisation (including payment-adjacent e-government services). Its pages point to dataset availability rules and to its own IT procurements.

source_name: Центар за граѓански комуникации (ЦГК) — мониторинг на јавни набавки
why_relevant: The leading civil-society monitor of public procurement in RSM. Publishes periodic monitoring reports and case studies of individual tenders (confidential contracts, unlawful advance payments, disputed execution). Case-study output is directly reusable A6 evidence and it names concrete authorities and suppliers.

source_name: opendata.mk — платформа за отворени податоци за јавни набавки (ЦГК)
why_relevant: CSO-run open-data platform republishing procurement monitoring datasets in open formats (e.g. the COVID emergency-procurement monitoring set). A structured, already-cleaned alternative view of ESJN data that can be used to validate or backfill scraped records.

source_name: skopjehacklab/e-nabavki — open-source scraper for e-nabavki.gov.mk
why_relevant: Community project whose stated aim is to make e-nabavki machine friendly. Documents the dossier endpoint and its Id/Level parameters — a direct shortcut to a working collection method for the portal, and a pointer to other civic-tech actors who may hold historical dumps.

source_name: EU Publications Office — Public procurement / TED, North Macedonia notices
why_relevant: IPA- and EU-funded procurements executed in North Macedonia (including e-government, payment and IT projects) are published here rather than only nationally. Structured, English-language, and machine-accessible — a complement to ESJN for donor-funded banking/payments IT.

source_name: Contracting-authority own procurement pages (Царинска управа, ЈП, министерства)
source_subtype: contracting authority mirror of tender documentation
why_relevant: Many authorities mirror tender documentation as PDFs on their own sites, often with fuller technical specifications than the ESJN summary. Customs, Ministry of Economy, Ministry of Defence and utilities (Vodovod Skopje, EVN) all do this. Technical specs reveal incumbent vendor lock-in and product names for payment/IT systems.

source_name: zanabavki.mk — практичар/консултантски ресурс за е-набавки
why_relevant: Practitioner-facing site with manuals for economic operators on preparing bids in the ESJN. Useful for decoding portal workflow, field names and procedure types, which improves parsing accuracy; also a pointer to the consultant community that tracks tenders commercially.

source_name: Слободен пристап (slobodenpristap.mk) — FOI request platform
why_relevant: Public FOI-request platform listing bodies (including ДКЖЈН and procurement authorities) and publishing responses. A legal fallback route to obtain award documents or contract annexes that are not posted, and an archive of already-answered requests.

source_name: Meta.mk — таг „Биро за јавни набавки“
why_relevant: Investigative/news outlet tag page aggregating reporting on the procurement bureau and contested tenders. Journalism surfaces award controversies and vendor relationships faster than the formal record and provides narrative context for case studies.

source_name: ПОВ Портал (ovp.gov.mk) — обврска „Јавните набавки како отворени податоци“
why_relevant: Open Government Partnership national action-plan portal carrying the commitment to publish procurement as open data. Tells you what machine-readable publication is promised, by whom and by when — i.e. where the ESJN data pipeline is expected to improve, and who to press if it does not.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU Official Journal Supplement)
why_relevant: TED coverage explicitly extends to the Republic of North Macedonia alongside the EEA and Switzerland, so above-threshold MK notices and contract award notices (with winning vendor name, value, CPV) surface here in English. Primary channel for spotting international payment/core-banking/ATM vendors entering MK via EU-visible procedures.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP)
why_relevant: Since the migration away from ebrd.com listings, ECEPP is now the ONLY publication channel for EBRD loan/grant-financed procurement, prequalification, shortlisting and contract award notices. EBRD has ~60+ projects in MK concentrated in the banking sector, so MK financial-infrastructure consultancies and IT supply contracts and their winners appear here.

source_name: EBRD Procurement Notices (corporate index page)
why_relevant: Index/redirect layer that explains what is published where and still exposes filterable notice listings and the guidance documents; useful as a pointer into ECEPP and into EBRD corporate (SMART by GEP) consultancy procurement.

source_name: EBRD — North Macedonia country page and project summary documents
why_relevant: Project Summary Documents name the client financial institution, instrument, and often the TC consultant, giving the upstream signal months before any procurement notice; EBRD has been investing in MK since 1993 with a Skopje office.

source_name: World Bank Finances One — Contract Awards in Investment Project Financing, North Macedonia
why_relevant: Structured, downloadable dataset (STEP-sourced, FY2020 onward) of every contract award under WB investment lending in MK: supplier name, supplier country, contract value, procurement method, project id. This is the single highest-yield machine-readable vendor-identity source in this cell.

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports — North Macedonia Procurement Plans (STEP-generated)
why_relevant: Procurement Plans list every planned package with description, estimated value, method and market approach BEFORE tendering — a forward pipeline view. P176366 'Building Effective, Transparent and Accountable Public Financial Management Institutions' (MoF) is directly on-topic for public financial infrastructure and IT.
